text:
maria: Trying to create a heterogeneous GPU node pool in europe-west3 for batch + low-latency workloads. Need A10G for cheap batch and H100 for low-latency embeddings. Can we do two instance types in one pool or should we create two pools with AZ affinity?

jun: GKE node pools can’t mix machine types inside a single node pool. You should create 2 node pools (e.g., h100 and a10g) and use labels/taints + pod nodeAffinity. Keeps autoscaler logic sane. :+1:

oliver: Agree — two pools. Also recommend pinning H100s to a single AZ to keep quota predictable. GCP GPU quotas are weirdly per-zone. I already opened a quota request (GQ-4127) for +32 H100s in europe-west3-a.

maria: Thanks. I’m worried about maintaining two autoscaler configs and bin-packing. Any CA tips?

kevin: Keep CA simple: one autoscaler per pool with min/max tuned. Label pools like pool=embeddings/pool=batch. Autoscaler handles each group independently. Also set reasonable scale-down thresholds so spot churn doesn’t kill long jobs.

asha: Example terraform node pool snippet we’ll use as a template:
```
resource "google_container_node_pool" "h100_pool" {
  name = "h100-pool"
  cluster = google_container_cluster.primary.name

  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-16"
    accelerators {
      type  = "nvidia-tesla-h100"
      count = 1
    }
    taints  = ["gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule"]
    labels  = { pool = "h100", gpu_type = "h100" }
  }

  node_locations = ["europe-west3-a"]

  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 0
    max_node_count = 8
  }
}
```

oliver: For A10G batch pool spread across az-a,b,c and use preemptible instances for cost. Keep H100s in az-a only (replicate later). Also add a node label `gpu_vendor:nvidia` etc so daemonsets can target specific driver installs.

infra-bot: quota-check: europe-west3-b H100 quota exhausted (usage 16 / limit 16). europe-west3-a has 8 / 16 in use.

jun: Driver note: different GPUs may require different CUDA/toolkit. Deploy `nvidia-driver-installer` daemonset with nodeSelector `gpu_type: h100` and another for `gpu_type: a10g` or use a single flexible installer that reads the label. Otherwise node boot failures will be fun. :thinking:

maria: For cost we plan: keep H100s on reserved/dedicated for embeddings routing, use preemptible A10Gs for batch inference. If quota or lead time blocks H100s, fallback to hosted Redwood API for embeddings until capacity exists.

kevin: Also add PDBs + checkpointing for batch jobs that use preemptible nodes. Consider node affinity weights so small latency pods prefer H100 pool but can fall back to A10G if allowed (and annotated).

asha: I’ll open a PR with two node pools + autoscaler configs + kube manifests for driver daemonsets and pod affinity examples. I’ll link the quota ticket (GQ-4127) and include a terraform plan. ETA: EOD.

oliver: One more operational tweak: set cluster-autoscaler flags to reduce thrash: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10` for spot-heavy pools.

maria: Great. If quota request stalls, plan B is: reduce per-pod embeddings batch size and route heavy requests to hosted fallback. Will coordinate with product. Thanks team :thumbsup:
